title: AI Parlance — AI-first IR for software generation
description: Write compact .aip specs. The reference toolchain parses, validates, and emits PostgreSQL, MySQL, OpenAPI, TypeScript, Go, and more. Clone the repo, run aip emit, less boilerplate.

hero.title: Intent first.
hero.subtitle: AI Parlance is an AI-first intermediate representation. Humans and LLMs write .aip; official emitters turn validated specs into SQL, OpenAPI, TypeScript, Go, and the rest of the matrix.
hero.note: Reference CLI in the monorepo: aip parse · validate · emit sql|openapi|typescript|go|mysql|…. Site playground below is illustrative only.

items.title: Smaller AI context
items.body: Edit ~10 lines of .aip instead of hundreds of framework boilerplate per entity.

items.title: Multi-target from one spec
items.body: One validated AST feeds PostgreSQL, MySQL, OpenAPI, TypeScript, Go, and more Preview targets.

items.title: Built-in domain blocks
items.body: Entities, CRUD, policies, workflows, and events in one predictable structure.

items.title: Validate before generate
items.body: aip validate checks full v0.1 tiers; aip emit produces Preview artifacts you can review before shipping.

items.title: LLM-friendly grammar
items.body: Controlled syntax helps agents produce consistent specs, not drifting code.

items.title: Honest scope
items.body: Focused on data-oriented APIs and automation — not custom UI or heavy algorithms.

postgresql.title: PostgreSQL from .aip — AI Parlance SQL emitter
postgresql.description: Generate PostgreSQL DDL (tables, FKs, indexes, seeds) from a compact AI Parlance spec. One IR, reviewable schema, less migration boilerplate.
postgresql.headline: Schema first. Migrations later — on purpose.
postgresql.sub: Describe entities in .aip and emit PostgreSQL you can read in code review. Indexes and seeds travel with the same source of truth.
benefits: Cut repetitive CREATE TABLE / FK boilerplate when iterating on domain models with an LLM or a human.
Keep naming consistent (plural tables, *_id) across SQL and other emitters.
Validate the spec before you touch the database — aip validate, then aip emit sql.
forWhom: Greenfield APIs where Postgres is the system of record
Teams aligning agents on a short domain file instead of huge SQL diffs
Reviews that need DDL without committing to a full ORM yet
notFor: A finished migration product with up/down history (Phase D deepens this)
MySQL apps — use aip emit mysql with database mysql
Running the database for you — you still apply SQL
postgresql.honesty: Strong on DDL, indexes, and seeds. Versioned migrations and soft-delete query semantics are still on the maturity checklist.

openapi.title: OpenAPI from .aip — AI Parlance contract emitter
openapi.description: Emit OpenAPI 3 schemas and CRUD paths from AI Parlance. Share one contract across backends, clients, and agents — less hand-synced YAML.
openapi.headline: One contract. Many consumers.
openapi.sub: CRUD entities become paths and schemas. api.prefix and app.auth feed the document so humans and tools negotiate the same surface.
benefits: Stop rewriting OpenAPI by hand every time an entity field changes.
Give agents a stable HTTP map instead of scraping route files.
Align path prefixes and auth schemes with the same .aip that drives SQL and TypeScript.
forWhom: API-first teams that treat OpenAPI as a deliverable
Specs where CRUD is the bulk of the surface area
notFor: Fully policy-aware per-operation security yet (tracked in docs maturity)
Replacing your gateway or rate-limiter product
GraphQL-only stacks (SDL emitter is a later option)
openapi.honesty: Excellent for schemas and CRUD paths. Policy→security enrichment and richer error models are Phase D work.

typescript.title: TypeScript from .aip — AI Parlance app emitter
typescript.description: Generate TypeScript interfaces and type guards from AI Parlance entities. Keep app types aligned with SQL and OpenAPI from one compact spec.
typescript.headline: Types that follow the domain — not the other way around.
typescript.sub: Emit Entity / Create / Update interfaces and zero-dependency guards. Path helpers hint at CRUD without locking you into Nest or Express.
benefits: Shrink LLM context: edit .aip instead of regenerating DTOs across the tree.
Stay consistent with PostgreSQL and OpenAPI naming from the same AST.
Start thin today; Phase D deepens toward runnable CRUD and stronger validation.
forWhom: TypeScript backends and full-stack apps on the happy path
Teams pairing agents with strict typecheck gates
Projects that want IR now and richer runtime emit next
notFor: A production server out of the box — handlers are not the MVP yet
Replacing your ORM (pair with emit sql / future Drizzle-style targets)
Ignoring Preview limits — see the docs scorecard before promising runtimes
typescript.honesty: Solid on types and guards. Runnable API, Zod-depth validation, and policy checks are the Phase D priority — tracked openly in docs.
